claims.claim: Israel is last in investment in early childhood (ישראל אחרונה בהשקעה בגיל הרך — posed as a question, answered by 'we dove into the data')
claims.verified_figure: Per secondary coverage of OECD EAG 2026: government expenditure per child aged 0-2, FY2023, Israel USD 1,482 (PPP) = 9.8% of OECD average USD 15,067; lowest among countries with data (UK 2nd-lowest, USD 3,093). For ages 3-5 / pre-primary Israel is below the OECD average but not reported as last (older EAG cycle: USD 5,853, 28th of 30). Israel's under-3 enrolment is among the highest (58.2%, 4th of 31), i.e. low public spending reflects a high parental share of cost (~82% parent-funded per Hebrew coverage), not low participation.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: Search summary of the Globes article: per OECD Israel is at the bottom on investment in education (in PPP terms), government investment more than 50% below the OECD average; 2026 review with 2023 data: USD 1,482 per child, the lowest of all countries with data.
claims.note: Judging the HEADLINE only (body_ok=0). 'Last' is supported for one specific metric — GOVERNMENT spending per child aged 0-2 — but the headline says 'investment in early childhood' generally. 'גיל הרך' conventionally spans 0-6, and Israel is not reported last for ages 3-5; 'investment' omits that the metric is public spending only (total incl. parents is higher). The undefined metric/age band changes what 'last' means, hence imprecise rather than accurate. Not 'overstated' because the body (per snippet) appears to state the narrower metric and the headline is phrased as a question. Primary OECD tables not read directly.
